messages:
sam: heads-up, after yesterday's kernel-selection autotune rollout i see a perf regression at 128-256 seq lengths. latency p95 up ~18% on colocated workloads. profiling attached below. :grimacing:
alia: ouch. which part regressed? kernel switch overhead or cache misses?
jordan: can you paste the flame graph? was the new kernel chosen more often for mid-seqlen?
sam: brief dump:
```
profile: requests 10k
seqbin 64: kernel A (old) hit 72% p50 18ms p95 34ms
seqbin 128: kernel B (new) hit 81% p50 22ms p95 54ms
kv-cache: hitrate seqbin128 41% -> 12% after rollout
batching: avg batch size down 1.3 -> 1.0
callgraph: increased time in kv-cache lookup + kernel select codepath
```
maria: interesting — cache hit drop is the smoking gun. did the keying change with the kernel hash added?
sam: yes. autotune now includes kernel_hash in cache key to avoid serving wrong kernel cached prefixes. seems that change fragmented the cache across kernels and pushed many misses.
kevin: fragmentation makes sense. we also changed persistence layout in the driver: we started versioning model keys at launch. combined effect -> new key prefix + kernel_hash -> nearly no overlap.
alia: that's rough. two problems: correctness (we need kernel_hash) and cache utilization. proposals: 1) versioned key prefix + kernel-aware cohorting (bucket by seqbin, allow kernel-agnostic fallback), 2) persistent migration (rehash or backfill), 3) debounce invalidation on driver rollouts so we don't wipe hot entries instantly.
jordan: I like cohorting. bucket keys as `<model_v>#<seq_bin>#<cohort>` and keep kernel_hash optional for exact-match entries. lookup should try exact then fall back to cohort match. fallback policy must be latency-aware (only use fallback if it doesn't increase inference cost).
maria: fallback correctness? if kernel produced different quantization outputs could we serve wrong KV? risk is small if both kernels are semantically compatible, but we need safety checks: store `heuristic_version` + `kv_schema_version` and a small checksum of prefix tokens.
sam: agree. let's add `compatibility_level` on cache entries: exact, compatible, unknown. runtime tries exact -> compatible (if checksum close) -> miss. compatibility_level is set by autotuner when it pins kernels.
kevin: persistence plan: don't mass delete. instead do a migration write-on-read: when a legacy key is read and matches compatibility, write the new key (atomic write) and continue. add a background scanner that promotes high-frequency legacy keys into new namespace. this avoids big invalidation waves.
alia: that's the debounce idea: when driver/runtime/model change happens, mark shard as `pending_invalidation` with a grace window (default 10m). during grace window, lookups consult both namespaces, but evictions prefer new namespace. only after grace do we mark old keys tombstoned and set TTL 1h for cleanup.
jordan: TTL choice? 1h might be long for memory pressure. proposal: tiered TTL: hot promoted keys get shorter tombstone (10m) because they will be backfilled quickly; cold keys get longer to reduce churn. also we need LRU vs LFU for cohort buckets — LFU seems stable for seq-skewed workloads.
maria: add metrics: per-seqbin hitrate, kernel-aware hitrate, fallback-rate, avg latency after fallback. capture before/after for rollout gating. we should reject canary rollout if fallback rate > 15% or latency p95 regresses >10%.
sam: good SLOs. i've a quick patch idea:
```python
# key format v2
key = f"m:{model_id}:v{model_version}:s{seq_bin}:c{cohort_hash}"
# optional exact suffix
if kernel_hash: key_exact = key + f":k{kernel_hash}"
```
lookup order: exact -> cohort compatible -> miss
```
kevin: for persistence backend (rocksdb) use a two-column family scheme: cf_exact, cf_cohort. migration on-read moves cf_cohort->cf_exact when checksum matches. snapshot cadence 5m and incremental compaction to avoid stalls.
alia: canary plan: ship logic server-side gate, enable for 5% of traffic with traffic-split by user_id hash. collect metrics for 2h, ensure fallback <= 10% and p95 within threshold. then ramp.
maria: perf test scenario: synthetic mix with seqlen distribution skewed to 128 and 256, both colocation and remote. measure kernel select CPU overhead, kv lookup latency distribution, and batching changes. also include cold start to capture migration-on-read overhead.
jordan: also instrument driver changes: when driver flips autotune parameters, emit event with `driver_change_id` so cache entries can note provenance and we can correlate invalidation spikes.
sam: i'll draft the PR for key schema + lookup fallback + migration-on-read. will include feature flag `autotune_cache_compat` and metrics. i'll also add the grace-window debounce config.
kevin: i'll prepare a small db-migration-runbook and an ops playbook if we see higher-than-expected miss storm. include a k8s rollout plan to limit surface area.
alia: thanks. also create a short eval harness to assert semantic compatibility across kernels before enabling cohort fallback default.
deploy-bot: Reminder: feature-flag rollout scheduled for 2025-05-12 18:00 UTC in staging.
sam: cool. i'll post PR link when ready. :thumbsup:
